{{Short description|German philosopher and writer (1770–1842)}}
[[File:Wilhelm Traugott Krug.jpg|thumb|Wilhelm Traugott Krug]]
'''Wilhelm Traugott Krug''' (22 June 1770{{snd}}12 January 1842) was a German philosopher and writer. He is considered to be part of the [[Kantian]] school of logic.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Lapointe|first=Sandra|title=Logic from Kant to Russell: Laying the Foundations for Analytic Philosophy|publisher=Routledge|year=2019|isbn=978-1-351-18222-5|location=Oxon|language=en}}</ref>

==Life==
Krug was born on June 22, 1770 in [[Radis]] near [[Wittenberg]] to a farming family.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last1=Klemme|first1=Heiner F.|title=The Bloomsbury Dictionary of Eighteenth-Century German Philosophers|last2=Kuehn|first2=Manfred|publisher=Bloomsbury Publishing|year=2016|isbn=978-1-4742-5597-4|location=London|pages=441}}</ref> He studied at the [[University of Wittenberg]] under [[Franz Volkmar Reinhard]] and Karl Gottfried Jehnichen, at the [[University of Jena]] under [[Karl Leonhard Reinhold]], and at the [[University of Göttingen]].{{sfn|Chisholm|1911|p=930}} After finishing his studies, he was employed as an [[adjunct professor]] at the University of Wittenberg.<ref name=":0" />

From 1801 to 1804, Krug was professor of philosophy at [[Frankfurt (Oder)]], after which he succeeded [[Immanuel Kant]] in the chair of logic and metaphysics at the [[University of Königsberg]]. From 1809 till his death he was professor of philosophy at the [[University of Leipzig]].{{sfn|Chisholm|1911|p=930}} He fought in the [[War of the Sixth Coalition|War of Liberation]] (1813–14) as captain of mounted chasseurs.{{Citation needed|date=March 2026}} He became Kant's successor at the University of Königsberg after the faculty of philosophy elected him to Kant's chair of logic and [[metaphysics]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|last1=Giovanni|first1=George Di|title=Between Kant and Hegel: Texts in the Development of Post-Kantian Idealism|last2=Harris|first2=Henry Silton|publisher=Hackett Publishing|year=2000|isbn=978-0-87220-504-8|location=Indianapolis|pages=293}}</ref>

He died in [[Leipzig]] on January 12, 1842.{{sfn|Chisholm|1911|p=930}}

==Views==
In philosophy, Krug's method was psychological; he attempted to explain the [[Id, ego and super-ego#Ego|Ego]] by examining the nature of its reflection upon the facts of consciousness. Being is known to us only through its presentation in [[consciousness]]; consciousness only in its relation to [[Being]]. Both Being and Consciousness, however, are immediately known to us, as also the relation existing between them. By this Transcendental Synthesis he proposed to reconcile [[Philosophical realism|Realism]] and [[Idealism]], and to destroy the traditional difficulty between transcendental, or pure, thought and things in themselves.{{sfn|Chisholm|1911|p=930}}

Krug challenged Schelling to deduce his quill or pen from [[German Idealism]]'s [[Philosophy of Nature]]. It was part of his empiricist objections to the new idealist philosophy.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite book|last=Stewart|first=Jon|title=Kierkegaard's Relations to Hegel Reconsidered|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=2003|isbn=0521-82838-4|location=Cambridge, UK|pages=637}}</ref> In so doing, he challenged the thinking that particular, perceptually real things could be logically known from general concepts. It prompted [[Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel]] to issue a critical response and forced him to deal with the issue of the knowledge of singulars.<ref name=":1" />

''Beiträge zur Geschichte der Philosophie des XIX. Jahrhunderts'' (1835–1838) contains criticisms of Hegel and [[Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling|Schelling]].{{sfn|Chisholm|1911|p=930. Reprinted in Krug's gesammelte Schriften, Neunter Band, Leipzig 1839}}

Krug was a prolific writer on a great variety of subjects, excelling as a popularizer rather than as an original thinker. His work stimulated freedom of thought in religion and politics,{{sfn|Chisholm|1911|p=930}} and he was a firm supporter of [[Jewish emancipation]].<ref>Gotthard Deutsch, S. Mannheimer, [http://www.jewishencyclopedia.com/articles/9534-krug-wilhelm-traugott# "Krug, Wilhelm Traugott"], ''[[Jewish Encyclopedia]]'', Vol. 7, New York 1904, pp. 578-579; [[Meyer Kayserling|Kayserling, M.]], [http://sammlungen.ub.uni-frankfurt.de/cm/periodical/pageview/3269175 Wilhelm Traugott Krug. Ein Blatt dankbarer Erinnerung], ''Allgemeine Zeitung des Judenthums'', 56. Jg., Nr. 3, 15. Januar 1892, pp. 28-30. ''See also'' Levy, A., [http://sammlungen.ub.uni-frankfurt.de/freimann/content/titleinfo/631737 ''Geschichte der Juden in Sachsen''], Berlin 1900, pp. 79, 91.</ref>

==Personal life==
In 1804, Krug married [[Wilhelmine von Zenge]] (1780–1852),<ref>{{Cite book|last=Loch|first=Rudolf|title=Kleist: eine Biographie|date=2003|publisher=Wallstein Verlag|isbn=978-3-89244-433-6|pages=232|language=de}}</ref> the eldest daughter of a Prussian major-general. They had six children. Wilhelmine had previously been engaged to [[Heinrich von Kleist]].<ref>[http://www.heinrich-von-kleist.org/en/heinrich-von-kleist/biography/ Heinrich von Kleist: Biography], Kleist Museum.</ref>

==Principal works==
*''Briefe über den neuesten Idealism. Eine Fortsetzung der Briefe über die Wissenschaftslehre'' (1801)
*''Entwurf eines neuen Organon's der Philosophie oder Versuch über die Principien der philosophischen Erkenntniss'' (1801)
*''Fundamentalphilosophie'' (1803)
*''System der theoretischen Philosophie'' (1806–1810):
**''Denklehre oder Logik'' (1806)
**''Erkenntnisslehre oder Metaphysik'' (1808)
**''Geschmackslehre oder Aesthetik'' (1810)
*''Geschichte der Philosophie alter Zeit, vornehmlich unter Griechen und Römern'' (1815; 2nd ed., 1825)
*''System der praktischen Philosophie'' (1817–1819):
**''Dikäologie oder philosophische Rechtslehre'' (1817)
**''Aretologie oder philosophische Tugendlehre'' (1818)
**''Eusebiologie oder philosophische Religionslehre'' (1819)
*''Handbuch der Philosophie und der philosophischen Literatur'' (1820-1821; 3rd ed., 1828)
*''Meine Lebensreise'' (1825, 2nd ed., 1842), autobiography{{sfn|Chisholm|1911|pp=930–931}}
*''Allgemeines Handwörterbuch der philosophischen Wissenschaften'' (1827-1834; 2nd ed., 1832-1838)
* ''Gesammelte Schriften'' (1830-1841; Collected works in 12 volumes): 
** 1-2: ''Theologische Schriften'' (1830)
** 3-6: ''Politische und juridische Schriften'' (1834-1836)
** 7-9: ''Philosophische Schriften'' (1839)
** 10-12: ''Enzyklopädische und vermischte Schriften'' (1841)
*''Universalphilosophische Vorlesungen für Gebildete beiderlei Geschlechts'' (1831)
*Beiträge zur Geschichte der Philosophie des XIX. Jahrhunderts (1835-1838):
** ''Schelling und Hegel oder die neueste Philosophie im Vernichtungskriege mit sich selbst begriffen'' (1835)
** ''Ueber das Verhältniß der Philosophie zum gesunden Menschenverstande, zur öffentlichen Meinung und zum Leben selbst, mit besonderer Hinsicht auf Hegel'' (1835)
** ''Der hallische Löwe und die marzialischen Philosophen unserer Zeit oder neuester Krieg auf dem Gebiete der Philosophie'' (1838)

For a bibliography of Krug's writings see his autobiography ''Lebensreise'' (1842, pp.&nbsp;343–360).
